draft.title: Anomalies in behaviour
card: An anomaly is behaviour that breaks a pattern or surprises us. A character has acted one way for most of a text, then does something quite different.
An example: a harsh landlord who has never shown mercy quietly pays a struggling tenant's rent. The reader does not expect it.
Because the act is unexpected, the reader stops and asks why it happened. The answer can reveal what drives the person, such as guilt, love or fear.
When you write about an anomaly, name the pattern first. Then show how the break from it reveals the character's motivation.
draft.remember: An anomaly breaks a pattern, and the reader asks why. The answer can show what drives the person.

a.q: In a novel, a coach is cold and strict to every player. One night he secretly drives a injured player home and waits with the family. Why is this an anomaly?
opts: It breaks the pattern of his cold behaviour
It repeats the pattern of his usual behaviour
It shows the coach is a minor character
It proves the coach is a kind person overall
a.why: The coach has acted coldly throughout, so a caring act breaks that pattern and surprises the reader. It does not prove he is kind overall: it only invites the reader to ask what drives him.
a.clue: Compare this act with how he behaves the rest of the time.

b.q: In a short story, Priya is known for boasting about her wealth. She then gives her prize money to a stranger and tells no one. What is the most likely effect of this anomaly on a reader?
opts: It prompts the reader to question what really drives her
It confirms that Priya is purely selfish
It shows that Priya's boasting was never real
It tells the reader the story is about money
b.why: The secret gift breaks her pattern of boasting, so the reader asks why she acted. This leads them to look beyond the simple judgement that she is vain. It does not show the boasting was fake: the text only invites a closer look.
b.clue: Ask what question the surprise makes a reader want answered.

a.best: It breaks the pattern of his cold behaviour

b.best: It prompts the reader to question what really drives her
